status_effects.explanation: Being turned away from by her husband toward other women marks a local diminishment in her emotional standing within the relationship.
His growing heaviness is narrated as the effect of the same vice affecting Saint-Loup, casting him in an unflattering light by association.

appraisal_events.evidence: Gilberte me parlait de Saint-Loup comme se détournant d'elle, mais pour aller auprès d'autres femmes. Et il est vrai que beaucoup encombraient sa vie.
appraisal_events.explanation: Gilberte reports that Saint-Loup turns away from her toward other women, a claim the narrator confirms as true, locally positioning her as neglected within the marriage.

appraisal_events.evidence: Sa vie ne l'avait pas épaissi, comme Charlus, tout au contraire... Au fur et à mesure que Charlus s'était alourdi... effet contraire d'un même vice.
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator attributes Charlus's growing heaviness over time to the same underlying vice that drives Saint-Loup's transformation, casting his physical change as a parallel, unflattering decline.
